topStories.headline: D8 Supervisor Race Upended: Yekutiel Drops Out After New Assault Allegations, Leaving McCoy With Clearer Path
topStories.dek: The presumptive front-runner for the Castro, Noe Valley, and Glen Park seat quit the race Thursday after a San Francisco Standard investigation surfaced two more accusers — and an avalanche of lost endorsements followed within hours.
topStories.body:
Manny Yekutiel suspended his campaign for San Francisco's District 8 Board of Supervisors seat on Thursday, October 1, hours after the San Francisco Standard published an investigation in which two men said he groped them at a Pride party in 2023. The withdrawal ended what had been widely viewed as a dominant candidacy: Yekutiel had the endorsement of Mayor Daniel Lurie, multiple city supervisors, and the local Democratic Party going into the final weeks before the November 3 election.

The new allegations closely mirrored an earlier complaint filed in June by political organizer Brad Chapin, who said Yekutiel had grabbed him in an unwanted sexual manner at a house party in 2020. Charges were never filed and Yekutiel denied it, but that first allegation had already strained some of his political relationships. When Ryan Clark and his partner went public with a near-identical account from a 2023 Pride club event, the political math changed within hours. Mayor Lurie withdrew his endorsement. Supervisors Bilal Mahmood, Stephen Sherrill, and Matt Dorsey followed. Outgoing District 8 Supervisor Rafael Mandelman, who had initially stood by Yekutiel that same morning, also pulled his endorsement by the afternoon.

"After a great deal of reflection I have made the difficult decision to end my campaign for District 8 Supervisor," Yekutiel said in a statement reported by Mission Local. "I am not admitting to having assaulted anyone, and some of the things that are being said about me are fundamentally untrue. But I am deeply sorry for any boundaries that I crossed."

Because the deadline to remove a candidate from the ballot passed in June, Yekutiel's name will still appear when voters go to the polls on November 3. He said he will cease campaigning. The practical effect is to give rival Gary McCoy — a former aide to Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi and a longtime Castro-area resident — a significantly clearer path to the seat that covers the Castro, Noe Valley, Glen Park, and Diamond Heights. Two other candidates, Michael Nguyen and Darshini Patel, remain in the race. The local Democratic Party chapter scheduled an October 11 vote to reconsider its endorsement of Yekutiel, a withdrawal widely expected to be formalized at that meeting.

topStories.headline: 52nd Castro Street Fair Takes Over the Neighborhood This Sunday With 'Where We Belong' Theme
topStories.dek: The annual free festival founded by Harvey Milk returns October 4 with live stages, hundreds of vendors, and a new visual identity — and Muni warns of significant street closures starting at 2 a.m.
topStories.body:
The 52nd Castro Street Fair fills Castro and Market Streets this Sunday, October 4, from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. Entry is free, with a suggested donation of $10–$20 at the gate to support the fair's nonprofit beneficiaries. This year's theme, "Where We Belong," celebrates the Castro as a place of connection, visibility, joy, and chosen family — a spirit organizers say has defined the fair since Harvey Milk founded it in 1974.

The 2026 visual identity was created by artist Ece Kalabak, with graphic design by Özgür Baltutan. The artwork appears across signage, merchandise, social media, and print materials. Hundreds of local artists, vendors, craftspeople, and community organizations will line the closed streets, and multiple stages will feature live entertainment, DJs, and dance areas throughout the fairgrounds.

The SFMTA will close Castro Street between 16th and 19th Streets, Market Street between Noe and Diamond, and several surrounding blocks starting as early as 2 a.m. Sunday morning. Muni routes F Market & Wharves, K Ingleside, 24 Divisadero, 33 Ashbury/18th Street, 35 Eureka, and 37 Corbett will all be rerouted. Riders should check the SFMTA travel updates page for alternate stop locations before heading out. An official after-party at The Castro theatre begins at 6 p.m., presented by Polyglamorous.

topStories.headline: Glen Park Takes Center Stage in SF's First-Ever 'Walktober' Festival All Month
topStories.dek: The Crosstown Trail's inaugural citywide walking festival has more than 40 guided outings lined up for October, with Glen Park serving as a hub for a canyon history walk, a pub crawl, a five-stairway tour, and a Bird & Beckett talk.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's Crosstown Trail has launched Walktober, a first-of-its-kind citywide walking festival for October 2026, and Glen Park is among the neighborhoods most prominently featured. Organized by the Crosstown Trail in partnership with Glen Park Beautiful's SF Stairway Month and dozens of other community groups, the festival lists more than 40 guided walks traversing the entire city.

Several walks are rooted in or pass through Glen Park. The Crosstown Trail Pub Crawl on October 6 starts at Glen Park BART Station. A guided walk titled "Plants and Birds and Rocks and Things: The Remarkable Histories of Glen Canyon Park," led by neighborhood historian Evelyn Rose, is scheduled for October 11 — RSVPs go to GlenParkHistory@gmail.com. Glen Park librarians are leading a brand-new neighborhood walk designed especially for Walktober on October 21. The month's capstone Glen Park outing is the "Truly Terrific: Tiled to Tiled Stairway Walk" on October 24, co-led by Glen Park Beautiful's Renee Berger, which visits five tiled stairways across the city, passes the newly mosaicked pillars of the Bosworth Pedestrian Bridge, and finishes at Glen Park Station. On October 27, Bird & Beckett Books & Records hosts a stairways talk as part of the series.

The Bosworth Bridge, completed in May 2026 and now the city's first tiled pedestrian crossing, forms a natural centerpiece for several Walktober outings. The bridge's five pillars were covered in approximately 404 square feet of Indigenous-patterned mosaics by Glen Park School students working with artist Ross Holzman, organized by Glen Park Beautiful. The Glen Park Association notes that the neighborhood's BART station — listed on the National Register of Historic Places — is also a meet-up point for multiple Walktober events, and that Glen Park Station, the bar regarded as the neighborhood's living room, will serve as both a starting and ending point for walkers throughout the month.

moreNews.headline: Angela's Organic Ice Cream Opens Castro Scoop Shop in Long-Vacant Former 7-Eleven Space
moreNews.body: Petaluma-based Angela's Organic Ice Cream opened its newest location at 3998 18th Street (at Noe) in the Castro in late September 2026, filling a commercial space that had sat empty since the 7-Eleven there closed. Hoodline reported the opening this week. The Castro had been without a dedicated ice cream shop since Castro Fountain and Double Rainbow each closed within a week of each other last year. The new shop, owned by Ignacio "Iggy" Garat and his mother Angela Pryor Garat, offers 21 signature flavors, five seasonal flavors, and six vegan options, along with sundaes, milkshakes, ice cream sandwiches, brownies, and cookies made in-house. Hours are Sunday through Thursday noon to 9:30 p.m., Friday and Saturday noon to 10 p.m.

moreNews.headline: Entour, Castro's 20-Year Men's Clothing Store, Closed at End of September
moreNews.body: Entour, the men's apparel shop at 2319 Market Street, closed at the end of September 2026 after two decades serving the Castro. Owner Jeffrey Wang announced the closure in August. The store originally opened in 2006 at 3600 16th Street beneath the Lookout bar before relocating to its larger Market Street space in late 2023. It built a loyal following among LGBTQ+ shoppers for its selection of t-shirts, swimwear, underwear, and accessories.
